module purpose: neorv32_bus is a set of bus helper blocks: a 2-to-1 switch with pending-request and lock-aware arbitration, an optional request/response register slice, an address-decoding gateway and 32-device I/O switch that fan requests out and OR responses back, and AMO helpers that sequence read-modify-write and reservation-set/store-conditional transactions. Across these entities the RTL decodes request addresses and AMO types, stores arbitration and monitor state, computes timeout and SC-failure conditions, and drives the corresponding bus requests and responses.

use-case flows.value: arbitrate between request ports A and B, retain pending requests, drive the selected shared request, and steer the shared response back to the selected port
retain bus ownership across locked transfers until the originating request drops lock
optionally register request and response transactions between host and device interfaces
decode a request address to ports A/B/C/X, fan the request out, and combine the selected responses
detect a timed-out outstanding gateway transaction and report it as an error response
decode a main I/O request to one of 32 device ports and combine device responses
capture a non-reservation AMO command and operands, read the original memory value, sequence execute/write phases, and gate the core/system handshakes accordingly
compute the AMO write-back data from the captured read value, write operand, and AMO command
track reservation-set / store-conditional state and gate a store-conditional bus request
report store-conditional failure in the returned acknowledge and data bits
clear arbitration, monitor, AMO, and reservation-control state on rstn_i = '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Shared-bus arbitration and dispatch state for selecting port A or B, retaining pending requests, and honoring locked transfers
conceptual assets.reasoning: The switch stores pending-request and arbitration state in `state`, `a_req`, `b_req`, `sel_q`, and `locked` (lines 55-67), then computes the current selection and request launch in the FSM (`sel`, `stb`, `state_nxt`, lines 83-134). Those decisions steer the shared request fields on `x_req_o` (lines 140-148 and, for data/byte-enable with generic conditions, lines 150-156) and steer the shared response back to A or B (`a_rsp_o.ack/err`, `b_rsp_o.ack/err`, lines 164-169). Integrity is established because corrupting this state or these decisions misroutes a request or response or violates the locked-transfer exit conditions (lines 88-92, 100-106). Availability is independently established because `a_req` and `b_req` retain observed strobes until the FSM can dispatch them (lines 61-67, 113-130). Under `ROUND_ROBIN_EN`, `sel_q` is also used to alternate priority (line 112). Transport ports are excluded, so the internal control state and decisions are the eligible structural references.

conceptual assets.concept: Gateway destination-port selection from the request address
conceptual assets.reasoning: The gateway computes `port_sel` from the request address and the enable/base generics (`A_EN/B_EN/C_EN/X_EN`) at lines 356-361. `port_sel` then qualifies `port_req(i).stb` so only the selected downstream port sees the request (line 378), and its X-port bit is latched into `keeper.halt` (line 416). Integrity is established because the routing flow depends on the decode choosing the correct destination; a wrong `port_sel` sends a request to the wrong downstream port or incorrectly falls back to X. The fan-out and combined-response records sit on transport elements, so `port_sel` is the eligible internal decision point.

conceptual assets.concept: Gateway timeout-supervision state and timeout error result for an outstanding transaction
conceptual assets.reasoning: `keeper.busy`, `keeper.lock`, `keeper.cnt`, and `keeper.halt` are updated by the bus monitor (lines 417-423) to track whether a request is outstanding, whether it was locked, how long it has been pending, and whether it was routed to the fallback X port (line 416). When the counter overflows and `keeper.halt = '0'`, `keeper.err` is asserted and the outstanding transaction is dropped (lines 423-425); that error is then ORed into the returned acknowledge and error outputs (lines 400-401). Integrity is established because this monitor state determines whether the gateway reports a timeout, suppresses timeout while halted, or releases a busy transaction on downstream acknowledge or lock release (line 426). Availability is independently established because the error indication is produced when the timeout condition occurs.

conceptual assets.concept: Atomic read-modify-write control context: operation phase, captured opcode, and captured operands used across the read/execute/write sequence
conceptual assets.reasoning: For non-reservation AMOs, the comb arbiter captures the opcode and write operand in idle (`arbiter_nxt.cmd <= core_req_i.amoop; arbiter_nxt.wdata <= core_req_i.data;`, lines 778-779) and moves to `S_READ_WAIT` (line 780). In `S_READ_WAIT`, it captures the returned read value (`arbiter_nxt.rdata <= sys_rsp_i.data;`, line 785) and advances on acknowledge (lines 786-787), then sequences `S_EXECUTE`, `S_WRITE`, and `S_WRITE_WAIT` (lines 792, 796, 800-801). These values are latched by the whole-record assignment `arbiter <= arbiter_nxt;` on the rising edge (line 763), and they control the outgoing system request and the returned core response (lines 813-828). Integrity is established because corrupting this control context changes which AMO is executed, what operands it uses, or when the helper issues and completes its writeback. Availability is independently established because progress through the sequence depends on the acknowledged transitions at lines 786 and 800.

The AMO ALU registers `alu_res` on the clock (lines 833-845). Its value is selected from the captured opcode (`arbiter.cmd`, line 838), direct swap/writeback (`arbiter.wdata`, line 839), arithmetic/logic combinations of the captured read and write operands (lines 840-843), or the comparison result built from `cmp_opa`, `cmp_opb`, `cmp_less`, and `cmp_res` (lines 850-853, referenced at line 844). During write phases, this registered result is sent out as the system write data (`sys_req_o.data <= alu_res ...`, line 813). Integrity is established because the AMO flow depends on the system receiving exactly the computed write-back value defined by lines 838-853. Availability is independently established because the result is produced on each rising edge while the helper executes the operation.

conceptual assets.concept: Reservation-set / store-conditional control state and store-conditional failure result
conceptual assets.reasoning: In the reservation-set helper, `rvso` classifies reservation-style AMOs from the incoming request (`core_req_i.amo = '1'` and `core_req_i.amoop(3 downto 2) = "10"`, line 935). The registered `state` then tracks the LR/SC sequence (lines 906-930): a load-reserved request enters state `"10"` (lines 926-927), a store-conditional request in that state either proceeds to `"11"` or fails back to `"00"` depending on `rvso` (lines 910-915), and acknowledge in `"11"` returns to idle (lines 920-921). `state` and `rvso` gate the outgoing store-conditional strobe at line 944, and `sc_fail` is latched when an SC is attempted without an active reservation (line 957). That failure is reported by ORing it into `core_rsp_o.ack` and the low data bit (lines 963-964). Integrity is established because LR/SC enforcement depends on the correctness of this state, this request classification, and this failure result; availability is independently established because the helper explicitly reports a failed SC instead of silently suppressing it.
